open_points.subject: Consumer services / read a project context
open_points.text: reads its context in the disclosure class its token allows; the full context only with a token that allows `personal_data` (R0-43)
open_points.question: Is there a reduced context for a service whose token does not allow `personal_data`, or is `context` refused to it, as the table says ('a caller whose token does not allow `personal_data` refused')?
options: refuse context without personal_data, as the table says
offer a reduced context projection per class
open_points.default_guess: Refuse, as the table and R0-43 say; reword the actor line.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Kernel authority
open_points.text: a service token that carries agent authority (R0-31)
open_points.question: Does Kernel ever call Registry on its own behalf, without naming an agent session (for example, publishing as a producer), or must every Kernel call name a registered session and stay inside its set?
options: every Kernel call is agent-authority and names a session
Kernel also holds plain producer authority outside sessions
open_points.default_guess: Every Kernel call names a session and is checked against its set.

open_points.subject: R0-23 narrowed vs R0-30
open_points.text: the staff credential becomes the owner credential, and no tool an agent runs holds it
open_points.question: May any tool hold the owner credential (the narrowing implies tools not run by an agent may), or does no tool hold it, as R0-30 says ('held by no tool, agent or service')?
options: no tool at all holds it (R0-30)
tools the owner runs, not an agent, may hold it
open_points.default_guess: No tool holds it; fix the narrowing to match R0-30.

open_points.subject: create a project / correct a project
open_points.text: a customer reference that is unknown or erased refused (R0-16)
open_points.question: Must naming a restricted customer (R0-51) or a customer whose relationship has ended (R0-57) also be refused in create and correct?
options: refuse restricted and ended customers in both
refuse only on create
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unknown, erased, restricted and ended customers in both actions.

open_points.subject: erase a customer's contact data
open_points.text: name, phone, e-mail and language are gone
open_points.question: Does the customer's kind (person or company), added by R0-37, survive erasure, given R0-06's 'nothing else'?
options: kind is erased too
kind survives
open_points.default_guess: Erase kind too; keep only the identity and the erased flag.

open_points.subject: R0-55 restriction scope
open_points.text: A restriction stops every operation that uses the restricted customer's personal data
open_points.question: Is the object's address of a restricted person-customer's project 'the customer's personal data', so that `context`, 'read a project' and 'list projects' to PresuPro and Portal stop carrying it?
options: address withheld from services while restricted
address still served; only contact data is restricted
open_points.default_guess: Restriction covers contact data only; the address keeps flowing to services cleared for personal_data.

open_points.subject: R0-54 import sources
open_points.text: the owner picks one for each import ... The first successful import into production closes the operation for good
open_points.question: Can both the VPS and the test-rig sources ever be imported, or does the first successful import from either source close import for the other one?
options: one import in total, from one source
one successful import per source, then closed
open_points.default_guess: One successful import per source; closed when both are done or the owner closes it.

open_points.subject: import projects with their identity
open_points.text: from the source the owner picks — the VPS or the test rig
open_points.question: How does the source data reach production: does Registry call the source instance (against R0-18, 'calls no downstream service'), or does the owner upload an export, and what authenticates it?
options: owner uploads an export file through the owner interface
production pulls from the source instance with a token
open_points.default_guess: The owner uploads an export file in the owner interface.

open_points.subject: import projects with their identity
open_points.text: the projects of that source under the identities they carry, with their customers (`customer_ref` kept), objects, rooms and pointers
open_points.question: What happens to source data that breaks vNext rules: customers without a kind, projects with an address but no object kind, and pointers whose type or owner service the specification does not declare?
options: refuse the whole import
import with defaults or placeholders the owner fills in
skip the offending items
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the whole import and list the violations, so the owner corrects the source and retries.

open_points.subject: owner interface sessions and requests
open_points.text: the owner sees the registered sessions in the owner interface
open_points.question: Which actions let the owner list registered agent sessions and pending access requests? The table has only per-session reads.
options: add 'list agent sessions' and 'list pending requests' actions
fold them into 'read the session's access'
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner action listing sessions, each with its grants and pending request.

open_points.subject: change the active project or revoke a project
open_points.text: or the project leaves the session's set
open_points.question: When the revoked project is the session's active project, does the session then have no active project?
options: active becomes none
revoking the active project is refused until it changes
open_points.default_guess: The session then has no active project.

open_points.subject: request access / read the session's access
open_points.text: request access to a project ... failure: —
open_points.question: Since R0-53 requires the named session to be registered on every agent-authority call, is a request from an unregistered session refused? And is the answer to 'read the session's access' for an unknown session a refusal or 'no access'?
options: refuse an unregistered session in both
answer 'no access' and drop the request
open_points.default_guess: Refuse requests from an unregistered session; reading access answers 'no access'.

open_points.subject: R0-56 holdback expiry
open_points.text: When that date comes, the need to keep the data is assessed again: the owner records a new ground and date, or the data is erased
open_points.question: If the holdback date passes and the owner records nothing, does Registry erase the data automatically, or wait? How does the owner learn that a holdback is due?
options: erase automatically at the date
keep until the owner decides, flagged as due in the owner interface
open_points.default_guess: Flag it as due in the owner interface; erase automatically if no new ground is recorded by the date.

open_points.subject: R0-37 audit
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant: every change, every personal_data read, agent-authority reads, refusals, sign-ins?
options: all writes and every personal_data read
all operations including refusals
open_points.default_guess: All writes, every personal_data read, every agent-authority call, sign-ins and refusals.

open_points.subject: R0-52 vs audit retention
open_points.text: Otherwise the record is deleted whole
open_points.question: Audit entries name the project, and a project id is not anonymous (R0-26), while the audit log is kept two years. Do audit entries keep a deleted project's id, or is it removed or pseudonymised?
options: audit keeps the id for its own retention period
the id in audit entries is pseudonymised on deletion
open_points.default_guess: The audit keeps the id until the audit's own two-year retention ends.

open_points.subject: read a project
open_points.text: the project card (any status, V1-7) with its object and rooms
open_points.question: Does the card name the customer by `customer_ref` only for services and carry contact data for the owner, given that R0-43 says no contact data leaves except to the owner?
options: services get customer_ref only; the owner gets contact data in the interface
the card always carries customer_ref only
open_points.default_guess: The card carries customer_ref only; the owner interface shows the customer's data from 'read a customer'.
